beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer; reconstructed Walker prompt from Bao's CHANGE-BRIEF.md (not a recorded session). Liam introduces himself.
beats.narration_text: Bonjour — this is Liam, in for Bear. Bao Xing's particle assignment, revised: two effects in a Godot game that already works, each tuned from what Bao actually saw, tested, taken down to the shader Godot generates, and priced on the CPU and the GPU. The game is Lanternfall. Here is the ask, rebuilt from Bao's change brief.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer. The framing a viewer arrives with ('particles are decoration') is corrected to what the film shows ('particles are feedback').
beats.narration_text: The short version. These particles are feedback, not decoration. Each one answers a real event in the game: a hit, a step, a new level. None of them may change a single rule. And the one change that counts was made because Bao looked at the game and said the sparks weren't enough.

beats.narration_text: What the assignment asks for, and what Bao's brief answers. Effect A, a burst of sparks on every weapon hit. Effect B, a short ember trail, only while the courier really moves. One change to each, driven by something seen in the running game, with a prediction and real frames before and after. Tests that read every setting back. And under the hood: the process shader Godot writes, and a price on the CPU and the GPU against a budget set in advance.

beats.role_note: Code beat (code-then-result-v1): effects/defeat_sparks.tscn lines 19-32 in source tree 14e6b2c, read verbatim; the next beat shows the result.
beats.narration_text: A particle system is one node that spawns many short-lived, slightly different copies, and it decides three things. Emission: when, and how many. Sixteen sparks, all on one frame, because explosiveness is one, each living forty-five hundredths of a second, from a single point. Process: how each one moves and changes. Spread one-eighty, speed from twenty-five, a little gravity; further down the file, damping, the scale curve and the colour ramp. Draw: what each one looks like. A three-pixel spark texture, through an additive material.

beats.narration_text: Those three decisions, in a real fixture capture of the current version. Emission puts all sixteen out on one frame, so the first frame is one white cluster: the additive draw adds overlapping sparks until they read as white. Process spreads them, slows them, and walks each one along the colour ramp and the scale curve: pale yellow through a quarter of a second, then shrinking orange specks. At four tenths of a second the last one is gone, because its lifetime ran out.

beats.narration_text: Effect A starts with a signal. The session's damage function, which every weapon calls, announces each hit and where it landed. This listener answers it. Line forty-nine drops the hit unless the game is playing and fewer than thirty-two bursts are alive. Then a fresh burst is placed at the hit, in world space, and restarted. A new node per hit is the brief's overlap rule: a second hit never cuts off the first.

props.title: One burst per hit.
props.source: godot/effects/particle_presentation.gd · lines 47–57 · source tree 14e6b2c · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _on_weapon_hit(at: Vector2) -> void:
	hits_seen += 1
	if session.state.current != GS.PLAYING or hit_bursts.size() >= MAX_HIT_BURSTS:
		return
	var burst := HitScene.instantiate() as CPUParticles2D
	add_child(burst)
	burst.global_position = session.to_global(at)
	hit_bursts.append(burst)
	burst.finished.connect(_on_hit_finished.bind(burst))
	burst.restart()
	hits_spawned += 1
output: the burst belongs to the presentation root, not the enemy, so it survives the kill

beats.narration_text: Effect B, the trail, is decided once per physics frame. Line one twenty-six measures how far the courier actually moved since the last frame. Holding a key is not enough. Line one twenty-seven sets a jump limit, twice a frame's walk plus four pixels, so a teleport or a restart never draws a streak. Line one twenty-nine emits only while playing, visible, and genuinely moving.

props.title: A trail that needs real movement.
props.source: godot/effects/particle_presentation.gd · lines 121–131 · source tree 14e6b2c · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if not is_instance_valid(session) or not is_instance_valid(trail):
		return
	_apply_policy()
	var current: Vector2 = session.player.global_position
	var distance: float = current.distance_to(previous_position) if have_position else 0.0
	var teleport_limit: float = session.player.speed * delta * 2.0 + 4.0
	trail.global_position = current + Vector2(0, 7)
	trail.emitting = session.state.current == GS.PLAYING and trail.is_visible_in_tree() and distance > 0.01 and distance <= teleport_limit
	previous_position = current
	have_position = true
output: reads session.player and session.state; writes only the trail

props.title: The celebration, on the card screen.
props.source: godot/effects/particle_presentation.gd · lines 59–70 · source tree 14e6b2c · Godot editor reconstruction
props.code:
func _on_leveled_up(_level: int) -> void:
	levels_seen += 1
	if session.state.current != GS.PLAYING or level_bursts.size() >= MAX_LEVEL_BURSTS:
		return
	var burst := LevelScene.instantiate() as CPUParticles2D
	_sync_overlay()
	level_overlay.add_child(burst)
	burst.position = session.hud.levelup_particle_anchor()
	level_bursts.append(burst)
	burst.finished.connect(_on_level_finished.bind(burst))
	burst.restart()
	levels_spawned += 1

beats.role_note: Result of B21. Recorded tool output (evidence/assignment-6/current-r2-validation, evidence/assignment-6/mutations) and the windowed mutation capture (captures/defeat_sparks/mutation-godot3-name).
beats.narration_text: Recorded output, on this exact source: nine suites, three hundred twenty-seven checks, no failures, with the original game's tests unchanged. Then the proof the tests are real. Rename one property to its Godot three name, and the scene still loads, the burst still fires, a little tighter, and only the test notices. beats.narration_text: The CPU price, from two separate runs on the current version: thirty-two live bursts add between five and ten hundredths of a millisecond a frame, against a budget of one. The trail's difference is so small that its sign flips between runs. Why trust a headless number here? Because these are CPU particles: the simulation runs on the processor even with nothing drawn. A GPU particle node would read near zero headless by construction, since a dummy renderer never runs its shader.
